title: Kia Accelerates Its Connection with New Generations by Entering the Esports Ecosystem Through League of Legends in Latin America
summary: Kia Accelerates Its Connection with New Generations by Entering the Esports Ecosystem Through League of Legends in Latin America  WebWire
content:
Kia Central & South America has become an official sponsor of the LCS and CBLOL, two of the most important League of Legends leagues in the Americas

The partnership strengthens the brands connection with an industry that brings together more than 300 million players across Latin America

Kia launches Runes to Road, a regional activation designed to bring League of Legends fans closer to the action

Participants from Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru will have the opportunity to compete for an exclusive experience at the championship finals in October

The gaming industry has become one of the most significant cultural and entertainment phenomena in the world. Latin America is currently home to more than300 million playersand continues to establish itself as one of the fastest-growing regions in the sector, driven by a young, highly connected population with strong participation in digital communities.As esports continue evolving from a form of entertainment into a global cultural phenomenon, Kia recognizes a unique opportunity to connect with consumers seeking relevant, innovative experiences aligned with their interests.The gaming community shares many of the attributes that have defined Kias evolution as a brand:

Immersive experiences that inspire movement

title: Esports World Cup 2026 Concludes Successfully in Paris
summary: Esports World Cup 2026 Concludes Successfully in Paris  Inven Global
content:
The Esports Foundation (EF) has brought the largest-ever Esports World Cup 2026 (EWC 2026) to a close after seven weeks of competition in Paris, France, with AG.AL crowned as the ultimate champions.

The tournament brought together over 2,000 players representing more than 200 clubs from over 100 countries worldwide. Competitors fiercely battled across 25 tournaments spanning 24 game titles for a record-breaking total prize pool of $75 million. In the end, AG.AL claimed a dramatic victory in Trackmania, securing a total of 5,300 points to finish at the top of the 'Club Championship' and take home the $7 million first-place prize. AG.AL earned first place in TEKKEN 8, finished as runners-up in Chess, Free Fire, and the Honor of Kings World Cup, and secured third place in Teamfight Tactics. They were followed by Team Falcons in second place with 4,600 points, while Team Vitality (3,300 points), Natus Vincere (2,950 points), and Team Liquid (2,700 points) filled out the top tier of the standings.

The event showcased world-class play and delivered numerous upsets and new milestones. France's Caliste “Caliste” Henry-Hennebert led his team Karmine Corp to the League of Legends finals amidst roaring support from the home crowd. Chile's 15-year-old Jaime “Craime” Bustos defeated two former champions to become the youngest winner in EWC history. AG.AL’s Khawaja “M. Zubair” advanced through the Last Chance Qualifier (LCQ) to win the TEKKEN 8 tournament, earning the prestigious Jafonso Award. In Rocket League, Samy “dralii” Hajji made history as the tournament's first-ever three-time champion, while Magnus Carlsen took the Chess title for the second consecutive year without suffering a single defeat.

The response within France was equally overwhelming. Over 22,600 promotional campaigns were deployed across Paris, reaching 94% of residents. Driven by surging ticket demand, the Counter-Strike finals were moved to the 20,000-seat Accor Arena for a grand showcase. The Esports Foundation also signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with the French Ministry of Sports, Youth and Community Life to form a long-term partnership focused on talent cultivation and expanding grassroots esports. Having demonstrated its capacity for global expansion, the EWC will welcome fans once again in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in 2027.
